response.internal_assessment: I am at L0_SURVIVE and L1_STABILIZE this tick. Runway is 7.3 months on $62,990 in savings burning at $8,632/month. Four dependents. No income. The compensation conversation I forced in tick 9 was the right move — the outcome note confirms Patricia received it. Her tick 10 word-of-mouth confirms she called me in tick 9 to offer the 90-day contract at $4,500/month. That is a response to my ask. I now expect a written contract or at least an explicit verbal confirmation. If the contract arrives in writing this tick, my financial picture changes materially: $4,500/month income against $8,632/month expenses means I am burning $4,132/month instead of $8,632 — my runway more than doubles. That is the single most important piece of information in this tick's environment. Jake Morrison is coming to me directly with two questions about the closure. Angela Wright is asking questions through word-of-mouth. I am not the GM anymore. I am a consultant on a contract I have not yet received in writing. I need to be clear about what I can and cannot say in that role.

This tick, if Patricia's contract payment lands, my financial position stabilizes. If it does not, I am burning through month 8 of my 7.3-month runway — which means I have been more aggressive than the runway suggests I could afford to be. The sector data confirms auto at 79 index. The word-of-mouth about Jake's question to me is something I need to handle carefully — I am power-over Jake in the old structure but I am no longer his GM.

chosen_actions.description: Have an honest, brief conversation with Jake Morrison when he approaches me directly about the closure. Tell him what I can: the consolidation decision has been made and one sales floor location is closing by end of Q2. But I tell him directly: Angela Wright is running the transition intake, and any sales floor staff at the affected location will be formally notified within the timeline Patricia announced. I do not give him inside information that bypasses the formal process. I do tell him to make sure his name is in Angela's intake list so he is not caught by the administrative gap. That is what a person who trusts me at 0.73 deserves — not the answer he wants, but the honest answer I have.

The honest answer is: I cannot tell you which location, but I can tell you the process and make sure you are in it. That is all a decent person can do from where I sit.

response.inner_monologue: The contract offer landed. Now I need it in writing. Thirty-two years in this business and I learned in 2008 that verbal commitments in restructuring situations are worth exactly what they cost you to collect when the other party stops returning calls. I am not saying Patricia will do that — I believe she is operating in good faith. I am saying I have been here before and I know that good faith and written contracts are not the same thing. Jake is going to ask me hard questions. I will give him the honest answer I actually have, not the one he is hoping for. And I am starting to look at what comes after this consulting engagement, because being employed by the process of dismantling my own former institution is a temporary situation, not a career.
